title: November Examination
instructions: This paper consists of FOUR questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Use the information provided for the accounting questions.

questions.prompt: Which arm of government interprets the law?
Which tax is added to the price of most goods and services?
Which source document is used when cash is received from a client?
The reward for capital is…
Which form of ownership has unlimited liability?
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Owner takes money for personal use

questions.prompt: Income decreases owner's equity.
Local government is responsible for supplying water to households.
Capital is recorded in the Sundry accounts column of the CRJ.
A cellphone costs R2 400 before VAT. Calculate the price including 15% VAT.
Name the THREE levels of government and give ONE service provided by each.
questions.memo:
✓ National: defence / grants / foreign affairs (1)
✓ Provincial: schools / hospitals (1)
✓ Local: water / electricity / refuse (1)

questions.prompt: In a community the labour force is 8 000 and 2 400 people are unemployed. Calculate the unemployment rate.
Describe TWO causes of poverty and suggest TWO ways in which the government helps to improve the standard of living.
questions.memo:
Causes (1 each): unemployment; low education; illness; inequality
Government (1 each): social grants; free basic services; RDP houses; no-fee schools; public works jobs

questions.prompt: Identify the factor of production in each: (a) a delivery truck, (b) the cashier, (c) the plot of land, (d) the owner who started the shop.
What is the national budget, who presents it, and when?
questions.memo:
✓ The government’s financial plan of expected income and expenditure for the year (1)
✓ Presented by the Minister of Finance (1)
✓ in February each year (1)

context.text: The following transactions took place at **Lindiwe's Tutoring Services** during June 2025:

items: 1 June: Lindiwe deposited R25 000 into the business bank account as capital. Receipt 001.
3 June: Paid R4 500 by EFT for a laptop (equipment). EFT 01.
10 June: Received R3 200 from learners for tutoring services. Receipt 002.
15 June: Paid wages of R1 800 to an assistant. EFT 02.
20 June: Lindiwe withdrew R500 for personal use. EFT 03.
28 June: Received R2 800 from learners for tutoring services. Receipt 003.

questions.prompt: Calculate the total of the Bank column in the Cash Receipts Journal for June.
Calculate the total of the Current income column in the CRJ.
Calculate the total of the Bank column in the Cash Payments Journal.
Calculate the bank balance on 30 June (the opening balance was R0).
Analyse the transactions of 1, 3 and 15 June using the accounting equation (show the effect on assets, owner's equity and liabilities).
questions.memo:
1 June: ✓ A +25 000 (bank) ✓ OE +25 000 (capital), L 0 (2)
3 June: ✓ A +4 500 (equipment) and −4 500 (bank) ✓ OE 0, L 0 (2)
15 June: ✓ A −1 800 (bank) ✓ OE −1 800 (wages), L 0 (2)

questions.prompt: In which column of the CPJ is the transaction of 20 June recorded, and why is it not an expense?
questions.memo:
✓ Sundry accounts: Drawings (1)
✓ It is money taken by the owner for personal use, not a cost of running the business (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how the totals of the CRJ are posted to the General Ledger.
questions.memo:
✓ The Bank total is debited to the Bank account (1)
✓ The Current income total is credited to the Current income account (1)
✓ Sundry items (Capital) are credited to their accounts (1)

questions.prompt: A business has assets of R95 000 and owner's equity of R70 000. Calculate its liabilities in rand.
Classify each account as asset, liability, owner’s equity, income or expense, and state whether its balance is on the debit or credit side of the Trial Balance: (a) Equipment (b) Current income.
Explain the difference between limited and unlimited liability, and name ONE form of ownership with each.
questions.memo:
✓ Unlimited: owners are personally liable for all debts (1) ✓ e.g. sole trader / partnership (1)
✓ Limited: owners can lose only what they invested (1) ✓ e.g. private / public company (1)

questions.prompt: Thabo and Zanele want to start a car wash together. Recommend a suitable form of ownership and give THREE reasons for your choice.
questions.memo:
✓ Partnership (or private company, with suitable reasons) (1)
✓✓✓ Three valid reasons, e.g. easy to start; share capital, workload and skills; share losses; (company) limited liability and continuity (3)

questions.prompt: Name THREE qualities of a successful entrepreneur.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): creative; hard-working; risk-taker; confident; good communicator; perseverance; problem-solver

questions.prompt: Explain FOUR ways the government uses the money it collects from taxes.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): education; healthcare; social grants; police and defence; roads/infrastructure; housing; paying interest on debt

questions.prompt: Give TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of a public company.
questions.memo:
Advantages (1 each): limited liability; large capital from selling shares; continuity; professional management
Disadvantages (1 each): expensive/complicated to register; many legal requirements; must publish financial statements; slow decisions; profits shared
